GROK 4.5 IS WINNING ON COST EFFICIENCY

One of the clearest advantages right now isn’t just raw performance — it’s how much performance you get per dollar.

Grok 4.5 is currently leading in cost-efficiency rankings across multiple real-world coding and agentic benchmarks. In several tests it delivers results comparable to (or better than) top competitors while using significantly fewer resources.
On some workloads it’s delivering the same quality at a fraction of the cost of Claude and GPT models.
In a world where AI spend is scaling fast, efficiency is becoming just as important as peak capability.
Grok 4.5 isn’t only competing on intelligence. It’s competing on sustainable intelligence.

WHY THE STARSHIP CATCH MATTERS
Catching the Super Heavy booster with the tower arms isn’t just a cool stunt — it’s the key that unlocks true rapid reusability.

Here’s why it’s so important:

• Speed of reuse
Landing in the ocean or on a droneship still requires recovery ships, transport back to the pad, and significant refurbishment. Catching the booster directly at the launch tower means it can potentially be restacked and flown again in hours or days instead of weeks.
• Cost
The rocket is the most expensive part of spaceflight. If you can catch and reuse the booster with minimal work, the cost per kilogram to orbit drops dramatically. This is the path to Starship’s target of under $100/kg.
• Flight cadence
A multiplanetary civilization and large-scale orbital industry require flying often. High cadence only becomes realistic when both the booster and ship can be turned around quickly. The tower catch is what makes that possible for the first stage.
• Closing the loop
Falcon 9 proved reuse works. Starship aims for both stages to be fully and rapidly reusable. Catching the booster is the biggest remaining milestone for the first stage.
Everything else — Mars missions, lunar bases, orbital data centers, heavy cargo — becomes far more practical once you can catch the booster and fly it again quickly.

WHY DATA CENTERS ARE MORE EFFICIENT IN SPACE

Putting large-scale compute in orbit isn’t just sci-fi — it solves several of the hardest problems facing terrestrial data centers.

Here’s why space wins on efficiency:
• Cooling
On Earth, cooling is one of the biggest costs and constraints. Data centers consume enormous amounts of energy and water just to reject heat. In space, you can radiate heat directly into the cold vacuum. It’s a fundamentally better thermal environment.
• Power
Solar energy in orbit is continuous and more intense (no clouds, no night in certain orbits, no atmospheric losses). You can generate far more reliable power per panel than on the ground.
• Scale
Earth has limits — land, local power grids, water, and community opposition. Space does not. Once you can launch mass cheaply with Starship, you can scale compute far beyond what is practical on Earth.
• Energy abundance
The Sun produces vastly more energy than all of human civilization currently uses. Capturing even a tiny fraction of that energy in space for AI compute changes the entire scaling equation.
The main trade-off is latency, so real-time applications may stay on Earth. But for training large models, batch processing, and non-latency-sensitive workloads, orbital data centers have major structural advantages.
Cheap launch + abundant solar + easy heat rejection = a new ceiling for how far AI compute can scale.

BREAKING: Tesla will open source the design and software of the Model S and Model X. 🚗⚡

• Elon Musk says Tesla plans to release the complete design and software for both vehicles.
• The move follows Tesla's 2023 open-source release of the original Roadster's engineering and diagnostic materials.
• Production of the Model S and Model X ended in Q2 2026, with factory capacity redirected to Optimus and Cybercab.
• Open-sourcing the platforms will make repairs, maintenance, and modifications easier for owners and independent repair shops.
• Engineers and researchers will gain access to real-world EV battery, powertrain, and software designs.

The decision continues Tesla's long-standing commitment to open innovation and supporting the broader transition to sustainable transportation.
